data.title: Ganciclovir & valganciclovir
data.summary: Antivirals & ART · Guanosine analogue (ganciclovir) and its oral L-valyl ester prodrug (valganciclovir)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Guanosine analogue (ganciclovir) and its oral L-valyl ester prodrug (valganciclovir)

## Mechanism of action
- In CMV-infected cells, phosphorylated by the viral UL97 kinase, then by host kinases → triphosphate inhibits viral DNA polymerase
- Much more active against CMV than acyclovir

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- CMV infections in immunocompromised patients (retinitis, colitis, pneumonitis, CMV cutaneous ulcers in HIV/transplant)
- Prevention of CMV in transplant recipients
- HHV-6/CMV reactivation in severe DRESS (selected cases)

## Dose & formulations
- Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV every 12 h (induction), then 5 mg/kg daily
- Valganciclovir 900 mg twice daily (induction), then 900 mg daily; adjust for renal function

## Adverse effects
- Bone marrow suppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) — dose-limiting
- Renal impairment, CNS effects, fever, rash
- Carcinogenic, teratogenic and aspermatogenic in animals

## Contraindications
- Severe neutropenia (<500/mm³) or thrombocytopenia; pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Zidovudine, MMF, other marrow suppressants: more myelosuppression; imipenem (seizures)

## Monitoring
- CBC 2–3 times a week during induction; renal function

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (teratogenic); contraception during and after treatment (men 90 days).

## Viva points
- Activated by CMV UL97 kinase
- Neutropenia is dose-limiting
- Valganciclovir is the oral prodrug

_Sources: Khopkar ch.3; Wolverton 4e ch.11. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
